summary: This session from Zadul-Ma'ad (Provisions for the Hereafter) Part 80 focuses on the etiquettes of speech and eating as teachings from the Prophet Muhammad's life. Sheikh Ali Mashhour explains how the chapters in Ibn al-Qayyim's work, though seemingly arbitrary, are connected by the overarching theme of proper etiquette (adab), particularly regarding the tongue and speech. The lecture emphasizes the profound power of words, noting that in our modern age of excessive talk, words have lost their value and meaning. Muslims are encouraged to speak less, choose words carefully, and understand that speech can lead people to paradise or hell. The session also discusses the importance of saying 'Bismillah' (In the name of Allah) before eating, which Ibn al-Qayyim considers obligatory rather than merely recommended.
